known_facts_book1: A little girl who once lived in Kansas and now lives in Ozma's palace as a Princess of Oz.
Reads the whole destruction of Pingaree and the finding of the Magic Pearls in Glinda's Great Book of Records while visiting the Sorceress.
Follows Inga's later adventures in Ozma's Magic Picture and is roused to pity and indignation by his helplessness in the Nome King's caverns.
Asks Ozma's leave to go and help, takes the Wizard for company, and crosses the Deadly Desert on Ozma's Magic Carpet, which unrolls before them as they walk.
Carries a covered basket containing a dozen eggs, knowing this makes her more powerfully armed than a regiment of soldiers.
Scolds Kaliko for trying to harm his guests, saying trying is just as bad if not worse, and stamps her foot at him.
Is the one who actually frees King Kitticut and Queen Garee, by beginning to lift the cover from the egg basket — Inga never manages it himself.
Brings the news, read in Glinda's Record Book, that King Gos and Queen Cor were both drowned in a storm at sea.
Warns Kaliko not to be wicked any more if he can help it, and writes down the words of Rinkitink's banquet song.

known_facts_book1: A cheery little man with a bald head and a winning smile, found planting shoe-trees in the garden when Dorothy comes for him.
Harnesses the Sawhorse to the Red Wagon, loads Ozma's Magic Carpet, and carries a little black bag of the tools of wizardry.
Had been to the Nome King's caverns before and conquered the nomes with ease, so is not at all afraid.
Stoops down and gazes into Bilbil's eyes and recognizes at once that the goat is under an enchantment — and identifies him as Prince Bobo of Boboland.
Knows the story of the cruel magician who transformed the gallant Prince years ago, and that a diligent search for him has been made without result.
Admits that with all his skill he cannot restore Prince Bobo, the magician being dead and the anti-charm lost, and says Glinda might be able to.
Is the only person besides Glinda present at the incantation that breaks the enchantment.

known_facts_book1: The lovely girl Ruler of the Land of Oz, who never leaves her palace in this book.
Gives Dorothy leave to go to the Nome Country, suggests she take the Wizard, and lends her the Magic Carpet.
Promises to watch Dorothy in the Magic Picture and to see she comes to no harm.
Is named by Kaliko as the one power he dare not offend, being far more powerful than he is.
Sees the liberation of Inga's parents in the Magic Picture and orders a splendid banquet prepared before the party arrives.
Has royal outfits made in advance for Queen Garee, King Kitticut, King Rinkitink and Prince Inga, so the Queen will not be shamed at the banquet.
Seats the animal guests at a table of their own, served the sort of food their natures require.

known_facts_book1: Ozma's Royal Sorceress, whose Great Book of Records inscribes all important events that happen in every part of the world.
Learns from the Record Book of the events in the Nome King's caverns and becomes especially interested in the enchantment of the Prince of Boboland.
Is summoned to Ozma's palace by her flock of sixteen white storks, arriving before the Red Wagon does.
Questions Bilbil long and earnestly about the manner of his enchantment, and persuades him that his misfortune will make him better beloved by his subjects.

Breaks an enchantment the Wizard cannot, through a deliberate chain: goat to lamb, lamb to ostrich, then — the direct attempt having utterly failed — ostrich to tottenhot, tottenhot to mifket, and mifket to the true Prince Bobo.
Allows no one present at the incantation except her assistant, the Wizard, because she is not positive of success.
Is described as the most complete mistress of magic who has ever existed, and as having taught the Wizard all the real magic he knows.
